summary:
Our project develops a machine learning-based Flood Prediction System that estimates flood probability using environmental, geographical, and socio-economic factors. We experimented with multiple regression algorithms to identify an effective predictive model and developed an interactive dashboard that allows users to explore flood-related factors, enter data, and obtain flood probability predictions.

The project addresses the challenge of flood risk assessment by using data-driven techniques to estimate potential flood risks and make predictions more accessible and understandable.

Floods threaten lives, infrastructure, and economies worldwide. Our project aims to support better risk awareness and informed decision-making.

As a future research direction, we aim to develop an integrated AI-powered framework that forecasts environmental variables and combines satellite observations with predictive models to enable more autonomous, proactive flood early warning, including identifying potential flood locations, estimating severity, and generating location-based alerts.
details:
Project Details

Our project is a Machine Learning-based Flood Prediction System designed to estimate flood probability using environmental, geographical, infrastructure, and socio-economic factors.

How It Works:
The system processes a structured dataset containing 20 numerical features associated with flood risk. We developed and evaluated multiple regression algorithms, including Linear Regression, Ridge, Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, to identify an effective model for predicting flood probability. The system also provides an interactive dashboard where users can explore relevant factors, enter input values, and view prediction results.

Tools and Technologies:
We used Python, Google Colab, KaggleHub, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost for data processing, model development, training, and evaluation.

Benefits and Intended Impact:
The project aims to make flood risk estimation more accessible, support risk awareness, and help decision-makers better understand factors associated with flooding. By providing data-driven predictions through an accessible interface, it can contribute to more informed disaster preparedness.

Creativity and Innovation:
Beyond conventional input-dependent prediction, our proposed future direction is to explore an integrated AI framework that can forecast environmental variables themselves and combine them with satellite-based observations. Our long-term vision is a proactive flood early warning system capable of automatically identifying potential flood locations, estimating their severity, and generating location-based alerts.

Key Factors Considered:
We considered prediction accuracy, feature relevance, model performance, data quality, usability, and the importance of making flood risk information accessible to users.
